segments.t: Right as the evening dinner rush begins and a banquet order comes in, the cooks execute their sabotage plan. One by one, Fedya claims a stomachache, Senya pretends he nearly sliced his finger off, and Lyova excuses himself to meet Timur, leaving Aleksandr completely alone.
Алло, Лёва, вас срочно Тимур зовёт.
Right, let's take their exchange slowly and unpack the Russian.
'Our dinner service is starting.' Underscoring his dinner on the spot, Lyova chooses "nachinayetsya" ("begins", from the root "nachinatsya") so Timur hears the exact meaning.
'Quick, head to the storage room.' Addressing the warehouse to Lyova, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 3 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'May I step out to the restroom?' Lyova checks firmly to see how Timur will answer on the spot.
'I nearly sliced my fingers off.' Addressing his fingers beside Lyova, Timur brings in "paltsy" ("fingers", from "palets") as the key Russian word here.
'Where is the first-aid kit?' Dwelling on the kit on the spot, Lyova links the Russian words directly in the present with no word for "am", "is", or "are" needed.
'Do you need any help?' Timur challenges curiously what Lyova is actually getting at here.
'All right, I will take the dish out and do it.' Talking about the dish in this beat, Lyova brings in "blyudo" ("dish") to make the meaning unmistakable.
'At table seven.' Discussing the table with Lyova, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 3 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
Алло, Лёва, вас срочно Тимур зовёт.
'Hello, Lyova, Timur is calling for you urgently.' Timur steps in at once on the spot, keeping the focus on what actually matters here.
'Table eight is ready to go.' Underscoring the readiness on the spot, Timur reaches for the Russian word "gotovnosti" ("readiness, doneness", built from "gotovnost") right at the center of the line.
'I have a banquet on my hands.' Pushing back dryly on the spot, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 3 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'And they are in no hurry to speed up.' Timur fires back right away without a pause, shifting the mood of the conversation in a single beat.
'Where is everybody?' Leaning in smoothly before Timur, Lyova links the Russian words directly in the present with no word for "am", "is", or "are" needed.
Алло, Лёва, вас срочно Тимур зовёт.

That wraps up this scene as as dinner service begins, Senya, Fedya, Lyova, and Louis all invent excuses to leave the kitchen at once, leaving Aleksandr completely alone with a flood of orders. Until next time!
